name: Lemon essential oil (inhaled)
short: Pregnancy (inhaled): no adverse-event data from nausea trials; Apgar p=0.051, direction not given (15 lemon-oil births). Others: no related events in trials of 104 and 60; 1 stroke withdrawal.
text: Pregnancy: no cited source reports adverse events, or their absence, in pregnant women who breathed in lemon oil for nausea. The abstract of the 100-woman randomised trial of lemon essential oil inhalation for nausea and vomiting of pregnancy gives no information on adverse events or on pregnancy or birth outcomes, and a 2026 systematic review of five studies of lemon aromatherapy in pregnancy calls it possibly safe without giving safety data. A 2022 systematic review of complementary treatments for nausea in pregnancy (aromatherapy, herbal medicine and acupuncture) found that fewer than half of the studies reported adverse effects, mostly mild and transient symptoms; it does not separate the lemon oil studies. The abstract of a 90-woman randomised trial of lemon and peppermint essential oils inhaled together for nausea and vomiting of pregnancy also gives no adverse-event data (a combination). The only birth-related measure comes from a randomised trial during labour in 45 first-time mothers (15 given lemon oil to inhale, 15 ylang-ylang oil, 15 controls): the babies' Apgar scores at one and five minutes did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.051 for both; the abstract does not say which group scored higher). Outside pregnancy (this entry covers lemon essential oil breathed in, as aromatherapy, not taken by mouth or applied to the skin): in a triple-blind randomised trial in 104 adults having heart bypass surgery, lemon inhalation aromatherapy (the abstract does not describe the preparation), given before and for 72 hours after surgery and compared with an odourless placebo, was followed by no aromatherapy-related adverse events; one patient in the lemon group was withdrawn because of a stroke after surgery, which the abstract does not attribute to the aromatherapy. In a non-randomised before-and-after study in 60 people prone to motion sickness, aromatherapy masks incorporating lemon essential oil (the abstract does not say whether other oils were included), worn during a bus ride, were followed by no intervention-related adverse events, and blood pressure and pulse stayed stable. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
